children: The stock market ended mixed Friday as Treasury yields reversed Thursday's retreat, with the 10-year note climbing back to the key 5.0% mark.
The S&P 500 (
) +0.2%, the Dow
-0.2%, and the Nasdaq Composite
Information technology
(+0.8%) and industrials
(+0.5%) led the market's gains, while utilities
(-1.4%) and materials
(-1.1%) lagged as the day's biggest decliners.
The stock market rebounded Thursday after Wednesday's selloff, which followed the Federal Reserve's first rate hike since 2023.
“This was a week of chaotic volatility in securities markets, a result of back-to-back FOMC and quarterly triple-witching events," said Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of
. "Next week we will see calmer heads begin the process of price discovery into year end.”
Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid said
the central bank's decision earlier this week to hike rates as inflation has outpaced the Fed's 2% goal for more than five years.
Elsewhere on the economic calendar, industrial production growth stalled in August, falling short of expectations, while August leading indicators slipped and missed the consensus.
The 2-year Treasury yield
rose nine basis points to 4.77%, the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield
increased seven basis points to 5.01%, and the 30-year Treasury yield
advanced four basis points to 5.34%.

title: Wall Street closes mixed as Treasury yields rebound
